comments.body:
## Incident 3 (same ticket, after remediation): verifier FAILs without itemizing a criterion

Following the remediation the verifier itself prescribes, the three ticket-record-shaped criteria
on `wailsome-unsure-asianlion` were tagged `[operator-attested]` with the concrete evidence named
(comment titles plus their COMMENT event ids), and the plan review was re-run — PASS, re-signed at
`cd95a58d7d`. The close was then retried.

It failed again, with a DIFFERENT and non-actionable verdict:

    Error: completion verification FAILED for cb91-1535-fe3a-47fc - 1 unmet criteria; not closing.
      - (unspecified): verifier returned FAIL without itemizing the failing criterion.

Ticket state at that moment: `status: in_progress`, 4/4 ACs ticked, 2 comments, all events
committed, nothing uncommitted in the tracker.

So across three runs against substantially the same ticket state the gate produced:

1. 3 unmet criteria, with stated evidence that was demonstrably FALSE (claimed zero comments and
   status `open` while the store held 12 committed events including two COMMENTs);
2. (after the prescribed `[operator-attested]` remediation) 1 unmet criterion with NO criterion
   named and no reason given.

This is worth weighing in the disposition. Under the "deliberate review-time snapshot" hypothesis
the run-1 verdict is explicable, but run 3 is not: the tag is the documented escape and it still
failed, silently. A verdict that cannot name the criterion it failed leaves an agent with no
remediation path at all — it is indistinguishable from a structured-output parse failure, and the
run's own logs carry `parse_structured: multiple candidates validated ... selecting the LAST`
warnings elsewhere in this session, so a transient parse failure surfacing as a FAIL verdict is a
third hypothesis worth checking.

Suggested extra check for whoever picks this up: does the verifier distinguish "the model returned
FAIL for criterion X" from "I could not parse the model's verdict"? If those collapse into the same
FAIL, a flaky parse silently blocks closes that should pass.

comments.body:
## Third incident (fixable-angular-caribou, d4c2-b67e-ab99-4410) — SAME root cause, different symptom

Reported while this fix was in review: caribou's close failed twice with "Evidence collection
reached its search boundary" on criteria whose evidence demonstrably exists on `main`. After an
evidence-anchor comment citing exact file:line locations was added, the RETRY GOT WORSE (2 unmet
-> 3 unmet). Plan review passed; only the completion verifier starved.

That "worse after adding evidence" shape is explained by root cause 1, not by a separate defect.
Measured directly against the tree the pre-fix close gate pinned
(`refs/heads/tickets` = 8b8d776f, the code repo's stale mirror):

    git ls-tree 8b8d776f d4c2-b67e-ab99-4410/  -> 3 events, 0 COMMENT events
    ls .tickets-tracker/d4c2-b67e-ab99-4410/   -> 13 COMMENT events

The verifier could not see ANY comment on that ticket, so the evidence anchors were invisible to
the run they were written for. Adding them could not help, and the retry simply re-explored a
stale, anchor-less ticket. Post-fix the same read returns all 13 comments including the anchors.

This is the second independent ticket (with wailsome-unsure-asianlion) whose close was blocked by
the stale pin, and the first where the staleness masqueraded as budget starvation rather than as
"no such comment exists". Whether caribou ALSO needs a step-budget change is a separate question,
now testable for the first time against a verifier that can actually see its evidence anchors.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Live validation of the fix — BOTH blocked closes now verify PASS

Run from the fixed build (Gerrit 1700), read-only `rebar verify-completion`, no `--force`:

- `wailsome-unsure-asianlion` (cb91-1535-fe3a-47fc) -> **PASS**, 4/4 criteria met, 0 findings.
  Pre-fix this ticket failed three times: 3 unmet criteria citing `comments: []` / `status: open`
  (both false against the store), then a bare FAIL naming no criterion at all.
- `fixable-angular-caribou` (d4c2-b67e-ab99-4410) -> **PASS**, 5/5 criteria met, 0 findings,
  metrics `requests=23 tool_calls=27 total_ms=108162`. Pre-fix it failed twice with "Evidence
  collection reached its search boundary", and got WORSE (2 unmet -> 3) after evidence anchors
  were added — because, as measured above, the pinned tree held 0 of its 13 comments, so the
  anchors were invisible to the run they were written for. The completed 23-request search shows
  the starvation was a symptom of searching for evidence the verifier had been told about but
  could not read, not an inherently insufficient budget.

Two different presenting symptoms — "the record does not exist" and "evidence collection reached
its search boundary" — one root cause. No step-budget change was needed for either.

# Stale ticket snapshot in the completion verifier — CONFIRMED DEFECT (plus a second, independent bare-FAIL defect)

## Disposition

Hypothesis 1 (**staleness defect**) CONFIRMED; hypothesis 3 (**a non-itemized FAIL is
indistinguishable from "no verdict obtainable"**) CONFIRMED as a SECOND, independent defect.
Hypothesis 2 (deliberate anti-gaming snapshot) REJECTED: the pin is deliberate, but its documented
purpose is reproducibility/signability and its docstring states the goal is to pin "the shared
store, **not a stale local copy**" (`repo_snapshot.py:546-548`) — staleness is contrary to intent.

### Root cause 1 — the close path pins the ticket store with no fetch

`close_precheck` calls the verifier with `fetch=False`
(`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:505-512`), justified in its own comment (`:502-504`) only
for the CODE ref (`HEAD`, always local). `resolve_gate_handle` threads the same flag into the
TICKET store pin (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:115`), and in `materialize_tickets`
(`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:568-576`) `fetch=False` skips `origin/tickets` and pins the
main repo's local `refs/heads/tickets` — a mirror that only advances on fetch. `.tickets-tracker/`
is a SEPARATE repository, so that mirror is arbitrarily stale (measured here: 6757 commits behind).
Reproduced deterministically, no LLM call — `materialize_tickets(fetch=False)` then
`show_ticket(cb91)` yields `{status: open, comments: 0}`, while `fetch=True` yields
`{status: in_progress, comments: 2}`. That `status: open` + `comments: []` is verbatim what
incident 1's stored `COMPLETION_VERDICT` cited as its authoritative evidence.

### Root cause 1b — the two halves of the gate read different stores

The fenced context given to the model comes from the LIVE store (`gate_ops.py:174,190`); the
model's own `show_ticket` reads the PINNED snapshot (`runner.py:335-337`). The prompt labels that
context `<untrusted_ticket_context>` and names `show_ticket` authoritative
(`completion_verifier.md:26-28`), so the model correctly preferred the stale snapshot.

### Root cause 2 — a FAIL with no findings is fabricated, not reported

`reconcile_verdict` (`completion.py:454-467`) coerces any non-`PASS` verdict to `FAIL`, then, when
`findings` is empty, SYNTHESIZES a placeholder criterion `(unspecified)` — exactly what incident
3's stored verdict shows. Unlike plan-review (unsigned `INDETERMINATE`, exit 2), completion
verification cannot say "I could not obtain a verdict".

## Implementation plan

1. **Pin the ticket store at the LIVE store's own HEAD.** `materialize_tickets`
   (`repo_snapshot.py:534`) resolves the sha from the live tracker repo (`.tickets-tracker`) HEAD
   when present — the state every other rebar read sees — so the pin is current-at-close by
   construction and the gate's two halves stop disagreeing. Still immutable-by-sha and signable.
   `fetch` keeps its meaning ("may I touch the network?"), applied uniformly to every caller:
   - `fetch=True` (`review-plan` via `operations.py:203`, standalone `verify-completion`, MCP):
     force an UN-throttled reconverge of the tracker with `origin/tickets` (the `_store.sync`
     implementation `reads.ensure_fresh` uses, called so the <=1/min marker is bypassed).
     `reconverge` returns `None` on success AND on every failure, so it yields no usable signal;
     `materialize_tickets` confirms the outcome itself with `git -C <tracker> merge-base
     --is-ancestor <remote>/tickets HEAD`. Exit 0 (at-or-ahead) => pin tracker HEAD. Non-zero, or
     the fetch / `rev-parse <remote>/tickets` failing => fall back to today's exact behaviour,
     `resolve_ref(f"{remote}/tickets", fetch=True)`, so "no content visible today is lost" holds
     unconditionally, not only when a throttle window is open.
   - `fetch=False` (close path): pin tracker HEAD as-is — current-at-close, never the stale mirror.
   - Tracker absent (CI, checkout-less): unchanged `origin/tickets` -> local-branch chain.
2. **Give completion verification a "no verdict obtainable" channel.** Indeterminacy rides on a
   NEW framework-set boolean `verdict_obtainable`, NOT a third verdict token: the `{PASS, FAIL}`
   vocabulary, its normalizing validator, and fail-closed blocking stay intact, and no token can
   be coerced away. Touch points, all of them:
   - `reconcile_verdict` (`completion.py:442`) — the rule keys on FINDINGS, since `gate_ops`
     populates `result["criteria"]` before delegating here, so a genuine fault can arrive with a
     criteria manifest. For a non-PASS verdict with zero `findings`: if `criteria` holds any
     `met: false` entries, synthesize real findings FROM them (named criteria, NOT a fault); only
     when no unmet criterion is identifiable from either source, set `verdict_obtainable=false`
     and emit a finding saying no usable verdict was produced, replacing the fabricated
     `(unspecified)`. `verdict` stays `FAIL`, so every existing consumer still blocks.
   - `gate_ops.completion_reconcile` (`workflow/gate_ops.py:297`), the workflow close-gate path
     that also stamps `certifiable`: inherits the marker by delegating to `reconcile_verdict`;
     asserted by a test. Such a verdict is never certifiable and never signs, as any FAIL today.
   - `completion_sidecar` (`completion_sidecar.py:323`): the marker rides onto the durable record
     so a fault is queryable afterwards rather than looking like an unmet criterion.
   - `close_precheck.py:543`: check `verdict_obtainable` BEFORE the `!= PASS` branch and route it
     to a distinct message naming it a verifier fault, with retryable exit 11 instead of 1.
   - `_cli/_llm_commands.py:383-389` — the standalone `verify-completion` exit mapping, which
     today flattens every non-PASS verdict to exit 1: route `verdict_obtainable=false` to the same
     retryable exit 11 `_llm_error_exit_code` uses, so a fault is retryable from either entry
     point.
   - `schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json`: document the optional boolean.
3. **Fix the misleading wording at its real sites.** The "does not exist" phrasing is
   model-generated, so nothing is deleted from the prompt; instead (a) `completion_verifier.md`
   gains an instruction that an absence seen via `show_ticket` must be reported as "not visible in
   the ticket snapshot I read", never as a claim the record does not exist, and (b)
   `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE` (`completion.py:54`) is reworded to match.
4. **Document the ticket-store pin** in `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` (today it covers only the
   code snapshot), cross-referenced from `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] The investigation is settled and durably recorded here: the
      `show_ticket` read path with its exact pin point, and the verdict (staleness defect, NOT a
      deliberate review-time snapshot). Evidence: the "Disposition" and "Root cause" sections of
      this description, each carrying file:line citations. Already satisfied by the text above;
      the remaining ACs are the code end-states.
- [ ] The pinned ticket snapshot reflects the live store at close time, with a regression test
      that fails before the fix.
- [ ] The `fetch=True` consumers are covered: a regression test proves a `fetch=True` snapshot
      still contains everything `origin/tickets` holds (including via the confirm-or-fall-back
      path). Tracker-repo-absent environments keep the existing resolution.
- [ ] A non-PASS verdict from which no unmet criterion is identifiable sets
      `verdict_obtainable=false` and is reported as a verifier fault with a distinct message and
      retryable exit, not as a fabricated unmet criterion — with a regression test covering
      `reconcile_verdict` and the workflow path.
- [ ] The unmet-criterion diagnostic distinguishes "not present" from "not visible in the
      snapshot read", and the ticket-store pin is documented in `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`.
